native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: SES (family socioeconomic status): its positive effect on BA degree completion (baseline ~0.36, probit) attenuates by ~66-109%, flips sign to negative (down to ~-0.2293) and becomes insignificant once race (Black, Hispanic) and academic characteristics (ASVAB test-score composite, class percentile) are added to the model.
native_result.WorkflowB: Hierarchical block regression (M1 social background -> M2 +race -> M3 +academic characteristics -> M4 +both) across linear-probability OLS (HC3), logit, and probit; standardized/beta and bivariate-baseline robustness sweeps to recover the quoted 0.3636/-0.2293 pair; SES identified as the only variable with a positive-significant baseline that collapses/sign-flips/becomes insignificant when race + academic characteristics are added.
